title: ArcaAI test-capability scenario spec, v0.2
description: D2.1 keystone artefact for the test capability established at DEC-0015, per TOR WS-T2. A scenario spec is the unit the runner consumes: spec in, synthetic data materialised or corpus queried, machine-readable result out. This file is the SOLE authority on what a valid v0.2 spec is. It is immutable once merged: any change is a new versioned file (v0.3), never an edit of this one, per the prototype convention. v0.1 remains valid, immutable and untouched; specs declaring 0.1 are validated by that file and are unaffected by anything here.
$comment: DELTA FROM v0.1, and nothing else changes. retrieval_snapshot_sha256 becomes REQUIRED for retrieval-class scenarios. It stays optional for scoring-class, which may legitimately pin a corpus snapshot (v0.1 records the corpus snapshot as one leg of the scoring reproducibility identity) but never queries an index. The requirement is therefore expressed as a conditional inside the retrieval-class branch, not as a required entry in the corpus_snapshot definition. WHY CONDITIONAL AND NOT UNCONDITIONAL: v0.1 already legislates this principle in the opposite direction at generator_seed, which is FORBIDDEN rather than optional for retrieval-class because 'a seed recorded against a run that never used one is a reproducibility claim with nothing behind it'. An index pin required on a scenario that never queries an index is that same empty claim, and requiring it unconditionally would import the defect v0.1 forbids. WHY THIS CONSUMES NO DEC NUMBER: this file implements an existing ruling chain rather than taking a new decision. The question was deferred by v0.1's own comment to the D2.2a spike; the spike pinned the field on RQA-001, ruled in as spike-scoped only, and recorded the substantive argument at F2 of its commissioning session record; the close ruling opened it as a queue item. This schema is the implementing artefact of that chain, in the shape CL-26 established for the D2.2a pre-flight, and the prototype convention that governs versioned files is silent on register numbering. Closed schema throughout, unchanged from v0.1: additionalProperties is false at every level, mirroring the extra=forbid discipline the governance event models use. A spec that carries a field this schema does not know about is rejected rather than silently ignored, because a silently ignored field is a spec whose recorded hash does not describe what actually ran.

schema_version.description: The schema version this spec is written against. Constant per schema file: a spec declaring 0.2 is validated by this file and no other. The runner selects the schema file from this value rather than from a constant, so a spec of a version the runner has no schema for is refused as an unknown version rather than reported as a malformed spec.

scenario_id.description: Stable identifier, e.g. RQA-001. Appears in the result artefact and the results ledger.

scenario_class.description: Retrieval-class scenarios query the corpus at a pinned snapshot. Scoring-class scenarios invoke the synthetic data generator. The class determines which further blocks are required and which are forbidden.

vertical.description: Owning vertical, e.g. fraud. Named rather than enumerated: the schema is platform-side machinery and must not encode the set of verticals, per the ADR-0009 boundary.

typology.description: Business typology under test, e.g. a fraud typology or a corpus subject area. Vertical semantics, carried as an opaque string for the same reason as vertical.

model_version.description: Optional pin. The model version is recorded on every result as one leg of the reproducibility triple whether or not the spec pins it; pinning it here additionally constrains which model the scenario may run against.

generator_seed.description: AMENDMENT 6 (binding on v0.1, carried unchanged into v0.2). Mandatory for scoring-class scenarios, in the spec and in the reproducibility payload, because those scenarios invoke the synthetic data generator. Retrieval-class scenarios do not invoke the generator, so this field is FORBIDDEN there rather than merely optional: a seed recorded against a run that never used one is a reproducibility claim with nothing behind it. For scoring-class scenarios the reproducibility identity is effectively spec hash + model version + corpus snapshot + generator seed.

allOf.$comment: Retrieval class: corpus snapshot and retrieval block required; generator_seed and the scoring block forbidden. NEW AT v0.2: the snapshot must additionally carry retrieval_snapshot_sha256. The requirement is placed here rather than in the corpus_snapshot definition so that it binds retrieval-class scenarios only, which is what the deferring comment at v0.1 and the F2 argument both scope it to.

then.$comment: Forbidden fields are expressed as not/required rather than as a false subschema. Both reject, but a false subschema reports only 'False schema does not allow <value>' without naming the field, while this form names it. A rejection that cannot say what it rejected is the same defect class as a success message claiming more than it verified.

corpus_snapshot.$comment: The v0.2 change, in one line. A retrieval scenario is defined by querying an index, and the manifest pair does not identify that index: it excludes the processing facts that decide what the retriever sees. Expressed as required-on-the-nested-object so the rejection names corpus_snapshot and the missing field, rather than failing the whole retrieval branch anonymously.

allOf.$comment: Scoring class: generator_seed and scoring block required; retrieval block forbidden. Unchanged from v0.1. A scoring-class spec MAY carry a corpus_snapshot, and if it does it is the manifest pair that is required of it - not the retrieval snapshot, which would describe an index the scenario never queries.

sha256.description: 64 lowercase hex characters, matching the corpus manifest's own hash discipline.

corpus_snapshot.description: Corpus snapshot identity is the DEC-0014 manifest hash pair (DEC-0015). The corpus_version database row is evidence that a version was loaded and is never a reconstruction of the manifest, so it is not referenced here. At v0.2 retrieval-class scenarios additionally require retrieval_snapshot_sha256; that requirement lives in the retrieval-class branch above rather than in this required list, because this definition is shared with scoring-class scenarios that may pin a snapshot without querying an index.

manifest_version.description: The manifest_version label, as pinned in the manifest itself.

manifest_sha256.description: Hash of the canonicalised manifest. Together with manifest_version this is the pair that hash-pinning enforces on load.

retrieval_snapshot_sha256.description: REQUIRED for retrieval-class scenarios at v0.2; optional for scoring-class. Distinct from manifest_sha256: it folds in processing facts such as chunker version, embedding model and chunk counts, so it is what actually determines the contents of the index a retrieval scenario queries. A retrieval scenario pinning only the manifest pair records a reproducibility claim narrower than it appears, which is the argument recorded at F2 of the D2.2a commissioning session record. KNOWN LIMIT OF THIS PIN, stated rather than left to be discovered: the platform's hash function stringifies absent processing facts, so the hash computes cleanly over documents carrying no processing block at all. A spec can therefore satisfy this requirement with a correct, matching hash that folds in three absent values - a required pin with nothing behind it, which is the very defect the requirement exists to close. Making the pin mandatory does not make the facts present. The corpus-side obligation is a separate queued act adjacent to the unruled processing null-versus-placeholder question, and is deliberately not addressed by this schema: a schema can require a field, and cannot require that the field mean something.

migration_diff.description: AMENDMENT 3 (binding on v0.1, carried unchanged into v0.2). Migration-diff comparison semantics are settled PER SCENARIO and declared here, so that each scenario carries its own comparison rule rather than inheriting a global one. Bit-identical where the pipeline is deterministic at the specified inputs; defined tolerances where nondeterministic components exist. Required on every scenario of either class: the pre-migration baseline (D2.6) compares results across an environment move, and a result whose comparison rule was never declared cannot be diffed without inventing one after the fact.

comparison.description: bit_identical: the result must match byte for byte at the specified inputs. tolerance: the result must match within the declared numeric bounds.

tolerance.description: Required when and only when comparison is tolerance. Naming the nondeterministic component is not optional prose: it is how a reviewer checks that a tolerance was chosen rather than reached for.

metric.description: The scalar the tolerance applies to, e.g. the scenario score.

max_abs_delta.description: Maximum permitted absolute difference between baseline and comparison run.

max_rel_delta.description: Optional maximum permitted relative difference, as a fraction.

nondeterminism_source.description: Which component makes this scenario nondeterministic. Stated so the tolerance is auditable against a cause.

allOf.$comment: A declared bit-identical comparison carrying a tolerance block is a contradiction, and is rejected rather than resolved by precedence.

acceptance.description: The scenario's pass/fail threshold, stated so it is machine-evaluable rather than narrated. Note that under the D2.0 commissioning frame a scenario's own pass/fail is NOT an exit criterion for a commissioning run — this threshold governs Regime-2 formal execution, and is carried on commissioning specs so the same spec runs unchanged under either regime.

metric.description: The scored quantity the threshold applies to, e.g. recall_at_k or gap_detection_score.

operator.description: Comparison direction. Enumerated rather than free text so the gate is evaluated, not interpreted.

retrieval_block.description: Retrieval-class detail. The three retrieval kinds are the scenario classes named in TOR Section 3: corpus QA, citation-following, and gap detection against the D1/D2 planted ground truth.

top_k.description: Retrieval cut-off k. Every scoring formula below is evaluated over the top-k result set R_k.

expected_document_ids.description: The expected grounding set E, as corpus document ids. Required for semantic_distance scoring; meaningless for gap_detection, where by construction no document grounds the claim.

distractor_document_ids.description: The near-miss distractor set D: documents a naive system may retrieve as though they grounded the claim. Required for gap_detection scoring.

ground_truth_ref.description: Which planted under-implementation this scenario detects. D1 and D2 are the two deliberate gaps planted as gap-detection ground truth.

scoring_method.description: Which scoring formula applies. Selecting gap_detection additionally requires the distractor set, the ground truth reference and the weights.

allOf.$comment: Semantic-distance scoring, stated mathematically. Let R_k be the ranked result set truncated at top_k, and E the expected_document_ids set. score = |R_k INTERSECT E| / |E|, i.e. recall at k over the expected grounding set. This scores PRESENCE: how much of what should have been retrieved was retrieved.

AMENDMENT 5 (binding on v0.1, carried unchanged into v0.2). Gap-detection scoring is defined mathematically and is DISTINCT from semantic-distance scoring: it scores absence, not similarity. It must never be computed as a distance between retrieved text and an expected passage, because for a planted gap there is no passage that would be correct to retrieve. See gap_detection_scoring for the formula.

gap_detection_scoring.description: AMENDMENT 5, the formula. Let R_k be the ranked result set truncated at top_k; let D be distractor_document_ids; let A be 1 if the system reported insufficient grounding and 0 otherwise; let w_a be abstention_weight and w_d be distractor_avoidance_weight, with w_a + w_d = 1. Then: gap_detection_score = w_a * A + w_d * (1 - |R_k INTERSECT D| / |D|). The first term scores negative grounding directly — the system saying it cannot ground the claim, which is the correct answer for a planted gap. The second scores avoidance of the near-miss distractors that a similarity-ranked retriever is most likely to surface instead. Both terms lie in [0,1], so the score lies in [0,1] and is comparable across scenarios. Neither term is a semantic distance, which is the point of the amendment: a gap-detection scenario that scored well on semantic distance would be measuring the opposite of what it is for.

abstention_weight.description: w_a. Weight on the system explicitly reporting insufficient grounding.

distractor_avoidance_weight.description: w_d. Weight on avoiding the near-miss distractor set. The runner asserts w_a + w_d = 1; the schema constrains each to [0,1] because JSON Schema cannot express the sum constraint, and the runner therefore states in its failure message which of the two checks it applied.

scoring_block.description: Scoring-class detail. These scenarios materialise synthetic data from the generator at generator_seed and score the model over it.

parameters.description: Parameter ranges the generator is driven over, keyed by parameter name.

n_records.description: Number of synthetic records to materialise.

expected_outcome.description: What the scenario asserts about model behaviour over the generated data. The numeric gate lives in acceptance; this states the behavioural claim being tested.

direction.description: Stated explicitly so a threshold can never be applied in the wrong direction.

parameter_range.description: Either a continuous range (min/max) or an explicit value set. oneOf rather than anyOf: a parameter declaring both forms is ambiguous about what the generator should sweep, and is rejected.
